🇲🇽📚 <u>COYOACÁN'S NEW UTOPÍA BEARS PONIATOWSKA'S NAME</u>

Mexico City has opened its seventh Utopía — the free community complexes that anchor the capital's social policy — in Coyoacán, named for writer and journalist Elena Poniatowska.

A 242-million-peso investment turned a 9,000-square-meter lot into a center serving 130,000 residents of 17 neighborhoods: a free Parkinson's therapy center, laundry, public dining hall, health and care services, and an immersive climate-change room.

🇲🇽📱 <u>META'S OWN DATA: 1 IN 5 TEENS FED BODY-HARM CONTENT</u>

As the Mexican government builds its case for regulating social media use by minors, Contralínea lays out the numbers Meta never wanted public.

From an internal study of some 240,000 users supervised by whistleblower Arturo Béjar: in a single week, one in five teens aged 13 to 15 was served content that made them feel bad about their own body, one in eight saw it over and over, and one in 11 was sexually harassed.

"These are design issues — an algorithm that captures attention. The more time you spend there, the more harm it does," Béjar warned at the President's morning conference. Infinite scroll, autoplay, recommendation loops: engineered addiction, aimed at children.

🇲🇽⚽ <u>MEXICO'S KIDS BEAT THE US — 15TH REGIONAL CROWN</u>

Mexico's Under-20s took the Concacaf title off the United States with a 2-0 win in the final — a brace from Cristóbal Alfaro — to lift their 15th regional crown and their second in a row.

On top of the trophy: the berth for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic tournament, with the U-20 World Cup ticket already in the bag. The pipeline keeps producing.

🇲🇽🌋 <u>MEXICO RETIRES THE "PASO DE CORTÉS"</u>

On International Indigenous Peoples' Day, standing in Santiago Xalitzintla on the slopes of the Popocatépetl, President Sheinbaum decreed that the historic mountain pass between the volcanoes will no longer carry the conquistador's name: it is now the Paso de los Pueblos Indígenas.

Cortés crossed there in 1519, fresh from the Cholula massacre, on his way to Tenochtitlan. "The peoples passed through here long before," Sheinbaum said. "Let us call this pass the Pass of the Indigenous Peoples."

The communities that guarded those forests for centuries before 1519 are the same ones leading Mexico's reforestation today.

📈🇲🇽 <u>ZACATECAS EARNS A RATING UPGRADE: FITCH RAISES THE STATE TO AA</u>

Fitch upgraded Zacatecas from AA- to AA on the national scale and HR Ratings from HR A+ to HR AA-, El Economista reports — citing sustained debt reduction, stronger own-source revenue and a financial surplus, with zero new debt and no short-term borrowing to cover day-to-day spending. Both agencies kept the highest possible marks on the state's outstanding credits. A Morena-governed state getting upgraded for paying its bills and saving — austerity with results.
banner: ZACATECAS: FITCH UPGRADES RATING TO AA

🐢🇲🇽 <u>MEXICO'S NAVY AND PROFEPA SECURE 10,000 SEA TURTLE EGGS IN LOS CABOS</u>

When some 140 olive ridley turtles came ashore at Playa El Médano in Cabo San Lucas, Mexico's Navy, Profepa and Conanp were already there. Roughly 10,000 eggs were secured in turtle camps under conservation protocols — safe from looting and illegal extraction — until the hatchlings can be incubated and released. Environmental enforcement with boots on the beach, in coordination with the Los Cabos municipality and the hotel sector.
banner: NAVY SECURES 10,000 TURTLE EGGS IN BCS

🏠🇲🇽 <u>CDMX VS PROPERTY-THEFT GANGS: RESTITUTION IN 15 DAYS, 20 DEDICATED JUDGES</u>

Mexico City is going after real-estate theft rings with a specialized unit of 20 judges, restitution of stolen homes within 15 days and judicialization in 30. The numbers behind the push: 1,846 investigation files opened from 1,966 complaints, 185 properties already returned to their owners, 84 more secured and 46 people arrested this year — including leaders of the "Los Rodolfos" ring. Brugada was blunt about officials who look the other way: "any case will have very serious consequences."

🇲🇽🚡 <u>CDMX BUILDS THE WORLD'S LONGEST CABLE CAR LINE — 200,000 RIDERS A DAY</u>

Mexico City's Cablebús lines 4, 5 and 6 are already 20% built and will hit 40% by the end of the year, backed by more than 17 billion pesos. Line 5 — 15.4 km from San Bartolo Ameyalco to Metro Mixcoac — will be the longest of its kind on Earth; line 6 will connect Milpa Alta with Tláhuac for 186,000 people in 46 colonias and pueblos. Brugada: "Reducing travel times is fighting inequality and time poverty. The cable cars give back hours of life."

🏫🇲🇽 <u>MEXICO'S CONGRESS TO THE SEP: TEACH AGAINST HATE SPEECH IN SCHOOLS</u>

Mexico's Congress approved a ruling urging the Education Secretariat to reinforce teaching against hate speech in schools across the country — human rights, equality and non-discrimination as classroom material. The approved text is blunt: hate speech "does not constitute a legitimate variant of freedom of expression." While the far right tries to import its culture war into Mexican classrooms, the legislature is moving to vaccinate students against it.
banner: CONGRESS TO SEP: TEACH AGAINST HATE

🗳️🇲🇽 <u>SOMOS MÉXICO, PARTY OF THE "PINK TIDE," ORDERED TO REBRAND BY THE INE</u>

The party founded by the "el INE no se toca" crowd just got reined in by... the INE. Mexico's electoral institute gave Somos México until August 30 to change its name, logo and color, ruling the name is no neutral label but "a composition of words with semantic and pragmatic weight" that suggests the party speaks for the entire nation — and that its MX emblem "induces the belief" of state backing. The party, whose ranks include ex-INE officials and detained ex-governor Ernesto Ruffo as counselor, says it is open to an audit of its financing.
